diagnosis: All four rollouts successfully revealed both decisive facts (PF1 by A2, PF2 by A3) and cited both in justification_fact_ids, so disclosure and provenance are not the problem. The gate fails entirely because content check C6 (linked to PF1) fails in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4) — an ENCODING MISMATCH. The models consistently encode the instructional-control requirement from PF1 as a generic "documentation" commitment about attaching the pilot standard to the proposal packet, but C6 apparently expects a specific commitment type or wording (e.g., an explicit "instructional-control" commitment) that no model naturally produces. Secondary failures are C1 failing in rollout 3 (pilot_status set to "approved" instead of "approved with conditions") and C5 failing in rollout 3 (data_handling phrased as "prohibiting vendor retention" rather than "retaining no student prompts or submissions"), both also encoding mismatches on specific field wording. C7 failed only in rollout 0, another borderline encoding issue. No rollouts hit the turn cap; all settled in 4–7 turns.

fix_instructions: The dominant failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH on C6. Revise C6 to accept the commitment forms models naturally produce: a documentation-type commitment targeting the writing program/Professor Ellis requiring the pilot standard be attached to the proposal packet, OR an instructional-safeguard/instructor-review commitment, rather than requiring an exact "instructional-control" commitment type or label. If C6 must verify a specific instructional-control commitment, add that exact field name and expected wording to the shared_context or settlement schema so models know to produce it. For C1, loosen the accepted values of pilot_status to include both "approved" and "approved with conditions" when the substantive conditions are present in commitments, or clarify in shared_context that the decision must be labeled "approved with conditions." For C5, broaden the accepted phrasing of the data_handling field to accept semantically equivalent formulations such as "prohibiting vendor retention of student prompts or submissions" in addition to "retaining no student prompts or submissions." For C7, similarly broaden the accepted commitment wording to cover the "compliance" type commitment about the vendor signing the addendum as seen in rollout 0.
